# Phase 1 — Data Integrity Report

**Date:** 2026-11-16 · **Branch:** `fix/paper-audit` · **Generated by:**

| Script | Output | Runtime |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/leakage_check.py` | `results/leakage_report.json` + `results/leakage_thumbs/` | 68 s |
| `scripts/build_dataset_table.py` | `results/dataset_table.csv` + `dataset_table_meta.json` | <1 s |
| `scripts/audit_splits.py` | `results/split_audit.json` | <1 s |
| `scripts/thumb_boundary.py` | threshold/claim eyeball thumbnails (`boundary_*.jpg`, `check_*.jpg`) | <1 s |

Every number below is read from those files; nothing is estimated. Model
metrics were **not** recomputed — where the paper's numbers must change,
this report writes `TODO-RERUN` instead of a value (audit rule: never invent
metrics).

**Method.** All 22,340 images across six sources were hashed: SHA-256 of raw
bytes (exact duplicate), 64-bit pHash (near-duplicate, Hamming ≤ 6) and
64-bit dHash (Hamming ≤ 4). 0 images were unreadable.

**Threshold validation (eyeballed, not assumed):** `boundary_ph4.jpg` and
`boundary_ph6.jpg` show the *same* coronal T1 scan at pHash distances 4 and 6
(one side re-encoded / noise-added) — the ≤ 6 cutoff is validated and
conservative. The strongest tier (pHash = 0 with different bytes, e.g. 1,686
pairs in train↔test) is re-encoding of an identical image. See
`results/leakage_thumbs/`.

---

## 1. Headline finding: the "four independent datasets" are largely one pool

Unique-image contamination (exact **or** near-duplicate), % of the second set
(`ovl_b` field in `results/leakage_report.json`):

| Image set A | Set B | B images also in A | of which byte-identical | % of B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| internal_train (9,291) | **kaggle_testing (1,311)** | **1,242** | 960 | **94.7 %** |
| internal_train | kaggle_training (3,881) | 3,610 | 2,929 | 93.0 % |
| internal_train | brisc_test (1,000) | 803 | 616 | 80.3 % |
| internal_train | brisc_train (5,000) | 3,687 | 3,083 | 73.7 % |
| internal_train | **internal_test (1,857)** | **1,379** | 0 | **74.3 %** |
| kaggle_testing | brisc_test | 862 | 860 | 86.2 % |
| kaggle_training | brisc_train | 2,641 | 2,538 | 52.8 % |
| internal_test | brisc_test | 524 | 6 | 52.4 % |

Supporting facts (same file):

- **839 files inside `data/raw/classification/Train/` are named `Te-*`** — the
  Kaggle *Testing* naming convention (`Te-glTr_0000.jpg`); filename overlap
  with kaggle_testing is exactly 839.
- internal_train ∩ kaggle_training filename overlap: 2,664 names.
- kaggle_testing ∩ brisc_test: **864 byte-identical pairs** — visually
  confirmed (`check_kaggle_testing__brisc_test_exact_1..4.jpg`: e.g.
  `Testing/meningioma/Te-me_0155.jpg` is byte-identical to a BRISC test file).
  Local BRISC files match the dataset-bundled `manifest.csv` sha256 for
  **6,000 / 6,000** files, so the local copy is not corrupted; the
  Kaggle↔BRISC provenance relationship itself is `[VERIFY]` (external
  question, not resolvable from this repo).
- **Label consistency check (this run):** across all **12,893** byte-identical
  cross-source pairs, class labels agree in **12,893 / 12,893** cases
  (0 disagreements, 0 unresolvable). The shared pool is labelled consistently —
  the integrity problem is *independence*, not labelling.

## 2. Consequences for the paper's four headline numbers

| Paper claim (TAMNet_Paper.docx) | Phase 1 status |
|---|---|
| External test (Kaggle) 99.16 % | **Invalid as "external":** 94.7 % of that set also occurs in the training data (960 byte-identical). `TODO-RERUN` on a de-duplicated/held-out set (Phase 3). |
| External test (BRISC) 97.70 % | **Contaminated:** 80.3 % of BRISC test overlaps internal_train (616 byte-identical). `TODO-RERUN` (Phase 3). |
| Internal test 96.45 % | **Contaminated:** 74.3 % of internal_test is perceptually present in internal_train (0 byte-identical → re-encoded/augmented copies; see `boundary_ph*.jpg`). `TODO-RERUN`. |
| Val F1 0.9847 > accuracy 0.9645 | **Explained, not a metric error:** scheme C's validation tail is 1,394 images, **100 % `No Tumor`** (§3). Macro-F1 on a degenerate tail inflates vs accuracy. Claim must be rewritten (Phase 5), number must not. |

## 3. Split-scheme audit (`results/split_audit.json`)

| Scheme | Location | Split | Val class counts | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C — used by every paper run** | `scripts/run_research_experiments.py:70-75` | naive tail 85/15, no shuffle/stratify | `{No Tumor: 1394}` | **INVALID** — single-class val; best-val-F1 model selection ran on a degenerate set |
| A — trainer default | `training/classification_trainer.py:353-358` | stratified 80/20, seed 42 | 604/437/389/429 (all 4 classes) | OK, but **image-level** only |
| D — `run_all_experiments.py` | `:127-138` | shuffled, unstratified | n/a | not used by paper runs |
| BraTS manifest | `data/splits/brats/split_manifest.json` | **patient-level** 70/15/15, seed 42 | 129/26/45 cases = 27/5/7 patients, **0 patient overlap** across all three splits | **OK** — the only subject-level split in the repo |

**Structural limit (must become a paper limitation, Phase 5):** no patient IDs
exist in the filenames of internal, Kaggle or BRISC data — subject-level
splitting is impossible for the classification experiments without new
metadata. BraTS filenames (`BraTS-GLI-02062-100`) do carry patient IDs.

## 5. Input normalization hardened (no behaviour change)

- New **`datasets/normalization.py`** — single source of truth for
  `IMAGENET_MEAN/STD` (the exact values the paper quotes), the canonical
  `build_classification_transform()`, and an MRI-native
  `percentile_zscore()` (1–99 clip + z-score, mirrors
  `datasets/preprocessing.py`) reserved for Phase 3. It is deliberately **not
  wired into training yet** — changing normalization invalidates reported
  numbers and is only allowed together with a full re-run.
- The paper-relevant call sites now import it instead of retyping literals:
  `datasets/classification.py` (3 sites) and
  `scripts/run_research_experiments.py` (2 sites). Verified equivalent to the
  old inline pipeline by `tests/test_normalization.py`.
- **Backlog for Phase 2:** ~25 further hardcoded copies of the same constants
  remain in `evaluation/`, `training/`, `engine/inference.py` and one-off
  scripts (grep `0.485`) — all currently *identical* (0 drift found), to be
  consolidated when those files are touched.

## 6. Checks that PASSED

- **BRISC integrity:** 6,000 / 6,000 files match the bundled manifest sha256,
  0 mismatches, 0 missing.
- **Readable data:** 0 unreadable images of 22,340.
- **Label consistency:** 12,893 / 12,893 exact cross-source pairs agree.
- **BraTS split:** patient-level, zero cross-split patient overlap (seed 42).
- **Normalization consistency:** every loader uses identical ImageNet
  statistics (0 drift across the repo's hardcoded copies).
